tagline: A canyon road with a brief career as a gallery.
intro: Malibu Canyon Road runs through the Santa Monica Mountains and a tunnel to meet Pacific Coast Highway beside Pepperdine University. Off the road, Malibu Hindu Temple brings South Indian architecture to the canyon country.

The tunnel once had an unexpected adornment. In 1966 artist Lynne Seemayer, working at night on ropes, cleaned the graffiti off the rock above its southern entrance and painted a sixty-foot nude there. The press called her the Pink Lady. Within a week a road crew had covered her in brown paint.

moments.title: Malibu Hindu Temple
moments.text: Off Malibu Canyon Road, the temple complex pairs an upper temple dedicated to Venkateswara with a lower one dedicated to Shiva.

moments.title: Malibu Canyon tunnel
moments.text: Above the southern portal the Pink Lady, done in heavy-duty house paint, outlasted fire hoses and paint stripper, then showed through the fading brown for years.

moments.title: Malibu
moments.text: The canyon road meets Pacific Coast Highway at Pepperdine, a campus left outside the city limits, at the college's own insistence, when Malibu incorporated.
